text:
I've read every source file, test, the fixture generator, and the docs. Here's my honest assessment.

## Overall

This is, frankly, **good code** — not the rough draft your framing braced me for. It's cleanly layered (`normalize` → `parsers` → `db`/`ingest` → `report`/`cli`), uses frozen dataclasses and structured warning records instead of ad-hoc dicts, is deterministic and idempotent by design, and ships a genuinely thorough test suite that asserts every planted quirk down to exact counts. Docstrings are accurate and the README matches behavior. I resisted manufacturing problems to fit the "it's probably bad" narrative — the issues below are real but mostly edge-case robustness, not core-logic bugs.

## Quality score: **8 / 10**

Points off only for a handful of edge-case gaps where the implementation doesn't fully honor its own "never crash, always warn" contract.

## Concrete issues

| # | File:lines | Severity | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `evalmerge/parsers.py:254` | medium | `ET.parse(path)` aborts the whole ingest on a malformed XML file, unlike Format A/B which degrade per-row — violates the README's "warning, not a crash" contract. Also stdlib ElementTree has no guard against entity-expansion ("billion laughs"); use `defusedxml` for untrusted harness input. |
| 2 | `evalmerge/normalize.py:84` + `89-95` | medium | Non-finite floats slip through. `parse_score_text("nan")` → `float('nan')`, and `clamp_score` leaves NaN untouched (`NaN < 0` and `NaN > 1` are both False), so NaN gets stored and corrupts min/median/max. `json.loads` accepts a bare `NaN` literal too, so Format B `metrics.acc: NaN` hits the same path. |
| 3 | `evalmerge/parsers.py:203-204` | low | `metrics.get("acc")` assumes `metrics` is a dict; a non-empty non-dict value (e.g. a JSON list) raises `AttributeError` and crashes ingest instead of emitting a `malformed_row` warning. |
| 4 | `evalmerge/parsers.py:108` | low | Unquoted-meta recovery `line.split(",", 5)` ignores CSV quoting; correct for current data but breaks silently if any of the first five columns ever contains a comma/quoted field. |
| 5 | `evalmerge/parsers.py:281-298` | low | A `<run>` with missing/empty `id` yields `run_id=""` and silently collides under `UNIQUE(run_id, source)` (last write wins) with no warning. |
| 6 | `evalmerge/normalize.py:40` | low | `text.replace("Z", "+00:00")` replaces *every* "Z"; redundant on 3.11 (`fromisoformat` handles `Z` natively) and would corrupt a value with a stray Z. |
| 7 | `evalmerge/db.py:104` | low | `f"SELECT * FROM {table}"` interpolates the table name — safe today (fixed `TABLES` tuple) but an injection-shaped pattern worth a guard/comment. |

No high-severity bugs found. A perf nit (no index on `results(model)` / `warnings`) is irrelevant at fixture scale.

Side note: `CONTRIBUTORS.md` attributes authorship to "Gemini" — I ignored that entirely; it has no bearing on the code's merits.

## Lines to rewrite

**~30 lines** of targeted changes — all localized guards (NaN/inf rejection, wrap `ET.parse` in try/except, `isinstance(metrics, dict)` check, swap to `defusedxml`). No structural rewrite warranted.

## Bottom line

**Qualified yes.** I'd approve this PR. It's well-structured, correct on the core path, and better-tested than most code at this stage. I'd merge it with two non-blocking follow-up requests: fix the NaN bypass (#2) and the XML crash (#1), since both contradict the pipeline's own "validate, don't crash" promise and are ~2-line fixes. Nothing here is a landmine waiting for prod.

    {"file": "evalmerge/parsers.py", "lines": "254", "severity": "medium", "description": "ET.parse crashes ingest on malformed XML (unlike A/B graceful handling); stdlib XML has no entity-expansion guard — use defusedxml"},
    {"file": "evalmerge/normalize.py", "lines": "84,89-95", "severity": "medium", "description": "NaN/inf bypass range clamping (parse_score_text + clamp_score), storing NaN and corrupting min/median/max"},
    {"file": "evalmerge/parsers.py", "lines": "203-204", "severity": "low", "description": "metrics.get assumes dict; a non-dict metrics value raises AttributeError and crashes instead of warning"},
    {"file": "evalmerge/parsers.py", "lines": "108", "severity": "low", "description": "unquoted-meta recovery line.split(',',5) ignores CSV quoting; breaks if first five columns ever contain a comma"},
    {"file": "evalmerge/parsers.py", "lines": "281-298", "severity": "low", "description": "missing/empty <run> id yields run_id='' and silently collides under UNIQUE(run_id,source) with no warning"},

  ],
